simple.meaning: בָּעַט (bâʻaṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to trample down, i.e. (figuratively) despise.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:15. The surrounding contexts include family line, offering, sacrifice, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּעַט (H1163) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּעַט (bâʻaṭ) / H1163 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:15, 1 Samuel 2:29 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked.

definitions.full: H1163. baat [ בָּעַט ] verb kick (so Late Hebrew, Aramaic בְּעַט , ) — Qal Imperfect וַיִּבְעַט Deut 32:15 ; 2 masculine plural תִּבְעֲטוּ 1Sam 2:29 ; — kick (only figurative of refractory Israel) Deut 32:15 (absolute); kick at (with בְּ ) 1Sam 2:29 . בְּעִי Job 30:24 see עִי .
